section: Telugu language and literature to the 14th century - Nannaya, Tikkana, Errana, Palkuriki Somanatha
subsections: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Rajaraja Narendra, associated with Nannaya Bhattaraka, ruled during which period?
accepted.x: Rajaraja Narendra is recorded as ruling from 1018 to 1061 CE. Nannaya served in his court at Rajamahendravaram.
accepted.tq: Use the close-date trap by distinguishing the patron’s reign from the poet’s century.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following titles is associated with Nannaya Bhattaraka?
accepted.x: Vaganusasana is one of Nannaya’s titles. Kavibrahma and Ubhayakavimitrudu are associated with Tikkana, while Prabandha Parameswara is associated with Errana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related poet–title pairs.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Nannaya Bhattaraka:
1. He served as court poet, teacher and adviser to Rajaraja Narendra.
2. He is associated with Rajamahendravaram.
3. He is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Telugu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Nannaya was associated with the court of Rajaraja Narendra at Rajamahendravaram and is called the Adi Kavi of Telugu.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements belong to the same historical personality before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Nannaya’s contribution to the Telugu Mahabharata is correctly described as:
o: The complete Virata to Swargarohana Parvas
The Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of Aranya Parva
The Adi, Sabha and the remaining part of Aranya Parva
accepted.x: Nannaya translated the Adi and Sabha Parvas and 142 padyas of the Aranya Parva. Errana later completed the remaining portion of Aranya.
accepted.tq: Use the precise numerical detail to separate Nannaya’s share from those of Tikkana and Errana.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents Tikkana Somayaji’s share in the Andhra Mahabharatamu?
o: The remaining portion of Aranya Parva only
The remaining 15 Parvas from Virata to Swargarohana
Adi, Sabha and part of Aranya Parva
The complete Mahabharata from Adi to Swargarohana
accepted.x: Tikkana translated 15 Parvas, beginning with Virata and extending to Swargarohana. Nannaya handled the opening portion and Errana completed the remaining Aranya section.
accepted.tq: Compare the three poets’ shares and identify the middle contributor’s continuous range.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Tikkana Somayaji was associated with which patron and political milieu?
o: Singama Nayaka of Warangal in the eleventh century
Prolaya Vema Reddi of Addanki in the fourteenth century
Manumasiddhi II of Nellore during the Kakatiya era
Rajaraja Narendra of the Eastern Chalukyas in the eleventh century
accepted.x: Tikkana was associated with Manumasiddhi II of Nellore and the Kakatiya-era political milieu. Prolaya Vema Reddi was the standard patron associated with Errana.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-patron trap by matching the poet with the correct ruler and period.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a title of Tikkana Somayaji?
accepted.x: Kavibrahma was a title of Tikkana. Vaganusasana and Shabda Shasanudu are associated with Nannaya, while Sambhudasa is associated with Errana.
accepted.tq: Test title attribution through a nearby-personality distractor.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Tikkana called his rendering of the Mahabharata by which name?
accepted.x: Tikkana called his Bharata rendering Prabandha Mandali. Harivamsam is associated with Errana, while Andhra Shabda Chintamani is a Telugu grammar treatise attributed to Nannaya.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the poet’s own designation of his work from titles of other literary works.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Tikkana is correct?
1. He dedicated his work to Hariharanatha.
2. He preached Harihara Advaita.
3. Ketana was his disciple.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tikkana dedicated his work to Hariharanatha, taught the unity of Shiva and Vishnu through Harihara Advaita, and had Ketana as a disciple.
accepted.tq: When all three statements describe connected aspects of one poet, test the complete combination rather than an isolated fact.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Errana (Errapragada) is correctly associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: Errana was the court poet of Prolaya Vema Reddi, whose capital was Addanki. The other pairs relate to different rulers or periods and are not the standard association for Errana.
accepted.tq: Use the court-poet and capital pairing to reject swapped patron associations.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which of the following works is associated with Errana?
accepted.x: Errana wrote Harivamsam. Indra Vijayam and Chamundika Vilasam are associated with Nannaya, while Andhra Shabda Chintamani is the grammar treatise associated with Nannaya.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched work after separating the works of the three Kavitraya poets.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following poets in chronological order according to their literary periods:
A. Errana
B. Nannaya
C. Tikkana

Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: Nannaya belongs to the eleventh century, Tikkana to the thirteenth century, and Errana to the fourteenth century. Therefore, the correct order is Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest poet first and then place the later contributors by century.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Nannaya was known as Adikavi and Vaganusasana, not Kavibrahma. Kavibrahma is a title associated with Tikkana.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped title–poet pair among otherwise correct literary associations.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Nannaya’s literary style is particularly associated with which of the following?
o: Champu style combining prose and verse
A prose style without Sanskrit metres
accepted.x: Nannaya pioneered the Champu style, which combines prose and verse. He also adapted Sanskrit metres to Telugu and used the Akkara metre borrowed from Kannada.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining stylistic feature rather than an extreme or exclusive description.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: The Akkara metre used by Nannaya was borrowed from which language?
accepted.x: Nannaya used the Akkara metre, which he borrowed from Kannada. This formed part of his adaptation of metrical traditions to Telugu.
accepted.tq: Test a specific literary borrowing through a close language-based distractor.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Nannaya’s contribution to Telugu literature are correct?
1. He set down rules of Telugu grammar.
2. His style is noted for Akshara Ramyata.
3. He used the Akkara metre borrowed from Kannada.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Nannaya contributed to Telugu grammar, is associated with Akshara Ramyata, and used the Akkara metre borrowed from Kannada.
accepted.tq: Combine grammar, stylistic and metrical clues to identify the complete set of correct statements.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Srinatha — Member of the Kavitraya
2. Potana — Member of the Kavitraya
3. Nannechoda — Member of the Kavitraya
Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Srinatha, Potana and Nannechoda are not members of the Kavitraya. The Kavitraya consists of Nannaya, Tikkana and Errana.
accepted.tq: Use the exclusion list to identify the option in which no confusable poet is correctly included.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Errana’s contribution connects the works of Nannaya and Tikkana in the Telugu Mahabharata.
Reason (R): Errana completed the remaining portion of the Aranya Parva left unfinished by Nannaya.

Select the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the assertion and the reason are true. By completing the remaining part of the Aranya Parva, Errana linked Nannaya’s opening contribution with Tikkana’s later translation.
accepted.tq: Test whether the stated completion of a literary section explains the connecting role attributed to Errana.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Sambhudasa is one of Errana’s titles. Nannaya is associated with Vaganusasana, Tikkana with Kavibrahma, and Errana also with Prabandha Parameswara.
accepted.tq: Confirm one reliable title pairing and eliminate the options formed by swapping titles among the poets.
accepted.sec: Kavitraya - members, parvas, first translator, titles
